Every kit exposes **one theme value** with the same field names, cased for the language
(`colorScheme` in TypeScript, Swift and Kotlin; `color_scheme` in Python and GDScript). Every field
is optional. An empty theme is the Polaris Key look in the product's accent.

## The theme

| Field         | Values                                                                           | Default                                              | Meaning                                                                                                                                                                                                                        |
| ------------- | -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ |
| `preset`      | `"polaris-key"` · `"native"`                                                     | `"polaris-key"`                                      | The base look ([the native preset](#the-native-preset))                                                                                                                                                                        |
| `colorScheme` | `"system"` · `"dark"` · `"light"`                                                | `"system"`; `"dark"` for Godot and TV                | Follows the OS live, and is dark when the OS has no preference. Games follow their own art, so the Godot kit defaults to dark                                                                                                  |
| `accent`      | `"product"` · `"core"` · `"service"` · a color                                   | `"product"`                                          | The product's color, else one derived from its icon, else ink; `"core"` is Polaris violet. Every value goes through the [resolver](#the-accent-resolver)                                                                       |
| `serviceCues` | boolean                                                                          | `false`                                              | Service glyph tiles on settings group headers; implied by `accent: "service"`                                                                                                                                                  |
| `colors`      | a partial map of semantic roles (`surfacePage`, `textStrong`, `danger`, …)       | none                                                 | Per-role overrides, per scheme (`colors.dark`, `colors.light`)                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `radius`      | `"sm"` · `"md"` · `"lg"` · a number                                              | `"md"`                                               | The control radius; surfaces scale from it. On the web, `sm` is 6/10, `md` 12/22 and `lg` 16/28 (control/card)                                                                                                                 |
| `typography`  | `family`, `display`, `monoFamily`, `scale`                                       | Rubik (`"inherit"` when embedded), the kit mono, 1.0 | `family: "system"` uses the platform face and `"inherit"` the host's; `display` sets a heading face (games); `scale` multiplies on top of the OS text size                                                                     |
| `density`     | `"compact"` · `"comfortable"` · `"spacious"`                                     | `"comfortable"`; `"spacious"` for Godot and TV       | Control height and spacing only, never the component                                                                                                                                                                           |
| `motion`      | `"system"` · `"reduced"` · `"none"`                                              | `"system"`                                           | `system` follows the OS reduced-motion setting                                                                                                                                                                                 |
| `ambient`     | boolean                                                                          | `true` (`false` under `native`)                      | The product's own icon or art, blurred behind the gate and boot screens                                                                                                                                                        |
| `product`     | `ProductIdentity`                                                                | from the presentation, then the bundle               | [Product identity](#product-identity), including `shortName`, `wordmark` and `deviceCodeUrl`                                                                                                                                   |
| `copy`        | a partial map of copy keys, or a `locale`                                        | the OS locale                                        | [Localization](/docs/build/ui/localization/#overriding-copy)                                                                                                                                                                   |
| `poweredBy`   | `false` · `true` · `"line"` · `"badge"`                                          | `false`                                              | The optional "Powered by Polaris Locker" line (`true` means `"line"`) at the foot of AccountAndLicense, settings and About; `"badge"` draws the 320 × 104 badge on About where 320 px are free, else the line. Never on a gate |
| `platform`    | `"auto"` · `"ios"` · `"android"` · `"macos"` · `"windows"` · `"linux"` · `"web"` | `"auto"`                                             | Web and Qt Quick kits render that platform's variant inside a webview or QML (Electron on Windows gets Fluent, Tauri on macOS gets the Mac sheet)                                                                              |

## Where each kit takes it

Each kit has a tab with its badge. A kit that has not built the theme API says **Not built yet**.

<Tabs syncKey="ui-kit">
  <TabItem label="React">
    <KitStatus kit="react" />

    `<PolarisKeyProvider>` has no theme props. Wrap kit components in
    `<PolarisKeyTheme theme={…}>`, or give an individual component its `theme` prop; an inner
    boundary layers over an outer one. A theme leaves product values unset to use the adapter's
    presentation source. Host CSS customizes `.pk-root` through `data-part`, `data-key`,
    `data-state` and scoped `--pk-*` variables. The kit's rules sit in the `@layer polaris-key`
    cascade layer, so host CSS wins without `!important`; React and the web components share one
    stylesheet and one `data-part` contract.

    The provider's presentation supplies the product name, accent and verified icon. The browser
    fetches the icon without credentials or redirects, checks its SHA-256 and shows it as a
    `blob:` URL, so a page with a Content-Security-Policy needs `img-src blob:` and `connect-src`
    for the image origin (`https://img.plrs.im`); a blocked icon falls back to the monogram.
    Desktop apps reuse the host's Node cache over the bridge.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Web components">
    <KitStatus kit="elements" />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Vue, Svelte, Angular">
    <KitStatus kits={["vue", "svelte", "angular"]} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="SwiftUI">
    <KitStatus kit="swiftui" />

    `.polarisKeyTheme(PolarisKeyTheme(…))` on any view above the kit: `preset` (`.polarisKey` or
    `.native`), `colorScheme`, `accent` (`.product`, `.core`, `.color("#…")`), `serviceCues`,
    `colors` (per role, per scheme), `radius`, `typography`, `density`, `motion`, `ambient`,
    `product`, `copy`, `locale` and `poweredBy`. iOS controls stay capsules at every radius.
    Beyond the theme: `PolarisKeyStyle`, one style per component in the manner of `ButtonStyle`
    (`.welcomeStyle(_:)`, `.activateStyle(_:)`, `.signInStyle(_:)`, or
    `.polarisKeyStyle(_:for:)`), whose configuration carries the state, its copy lines and its
    actions, and the kit's own body to wrap. See [SwiftUI](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/swiftui/).

    **Product presentation (shipped).** `PolarisKeyModel` maps the client's `presentation` to the
    product identity once, so the kit shows the product's name, accent and verified icon wherever
    the theme sets none. `client.presentationSource` is the seam; the icon is fetched without
    credentials or redirects, checked by SHA-256 and cached in Application Support.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="UIKit, AppKit">
    <KitStatus kits={["uikit", "appkit"]} />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Compose">
    <KitStatus kit="compose" />

    **Product presentation (shipped).** `PolarisTheme(presentation = client.presentationSource)`
    fills what the integrator leaves out: `logo` falls back to the verified icon, then the
    monogram; under `PolarisBranding.PolarisKey` the accent falls back to the product's
    (`accentDark` on a dark ground), then one derived from the icon. The icon is fetched without
    credentials or redirects and checked by SHA-256.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Godot">
    <KitStatus kit="godot" />

    **Product presentation (shipped).** The kit's name, icon and accent default to the product's
    presentation from discovery (`PolarisKey.presentation_source`), after `ui_product_name`,
    `ui_product_icon` and `ui_accent`: `accentDark` in the dark scheme, else `accent`, else one
    derived from the icon, else ink. The icon is fetched without credentials or redirects,
    verified by SHA-256, decoded only as PNG, JPEG or WebP (an AVIF or GIF original with no WebP
    sizes shows the monogram) and cached under `user://polaris_key/presentation/`. On web the
    browser follows a redirect itself and the hash still gates the bytes. Product names are drawn
    bidi-isolated.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Qt">
    <KitStatus kit="qt" />

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Terminal (Node)">
    <KitStatus kit="terminal-node" />

    `theme` in the options of the commander or yargs adapter (`registerPolarisCommands`,
    `polarisCommands` from `@polaris-key/node/cli/yargs`), or in `createKitContext` for a program's own commands.
    `PKEY_THEME=dark` or `light` pins the scheme and `NO_COLOR` drops color. Beyond the theme: the `symbols` restyle
    hook (`"unicode"` or `"ascii"`), per-role truecolor `colors`, and the styled parts and the
    `@polaris-key/node/terminal` primitives. What each field does in a terminal is on the
    [framework page](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/terminal-node/#theming). The product's name,
    developer and accent come from `client.presentationSource()` when the theme sets none.

  </TabItem>
  <TabItem label="Terminal (Python)">
    <KitStatus kit="terminal-python" />

    `Theme` (`polaris_key.ui.core`) as `theme=` of `register_argparse`, `polaris_click_group` and
    `polaris_typer_app`, with `PKEY_THEME=dark` or `light` and `NO_COLOR`. Beyond the theme: a
    unicode or ascii symbol set and per-role truecolor `colors`. What each field does in a terminal
    is on the [framework page](/docs/build/ui/frameworks/terminal-python/#theming). The product's
    name, developer and accent come from `client.presentation_source` when the theme sets none.

  </TabItem>

## The accent resolver

One algorithm in `@polaris-key/brand` (`resolveAccent`), ported to Swift, Kotlin, GDScript and
Python, turns any input color into the five colors a kit draws with, for each scheme. It adjusts
OKLCH lightness only:

- **`solid`**, the primary's fill: at least 3:1 on every surface;
- **`fg`**, accent text and icons: at least 4.5:1 on every surface;
- **`subtle`**, the tinted fill of a selected row;
- **`focus`**, the focus ring;
- **`on`**, the primary's label: at least 4.5:1 on `solid`. It prefers white, so the label is
  the same in both schemes; only light accents (yellows, oranges, light teals) flip to an ink
  label, again in both schemes.

When the product supplies no color, `deriveAccent` picks one from the icon: the most saturated
color that covers at least 8 % of the icon's opaque area, or nothing for a near-greyscale icon,
which falls through to ink. Status colors never change with the accent.

The resolver's output for the specification's examples, read from the shared test vectors every
port must reproduce exactly (`packages/brand/fixtures/accent-vectors.json`):

## The native preset

`preset: "native"` keeps the structure, flows, copy and spacing and hand the look to the host:

- **Web:** the host's font (`font: inherit`), `Canvas` and `CanvasText` neutrals, the host's accent
  from `theme.accent`, else its `accent-color`, else the CSS `AccentColor` system color; radii from
  the host; no ambient. It never hard-codes a platform blue.
- **SwiftUI, UIKit and AppKit:** system fonts, the app's `.tint`, system colors and materials,
  stock button styles.
- **Compose:** the host's `MaterialTheme`, dynamic color included, with the status colors mapped
  to the host scheme's error and a computed warning.
- **Godot:** derived from the ancestor or project theme.
- **Qt:** the platform `QStyle` (or the Qt Quick native style), with only spacing and the type
  hierarchy applied.

## Bring your own design system

Host design systems have no kits of their own. Use the `native` preset, or draw the screens with host components over the headless layer ([Your own UI](/docs/start/choose-your-integration/)).

## Product identity

The product is the hero of every kit screen: each screen and pane, in every kit, opens with the product header (the icon or monogram, then the name). A product with no name reads "Welcome". A kit's `ProductIdentity` holds `name`, `icon`, `developer`, and optionally `shortName`, `accent`, `art`, `wordmark` and `deviceCodeUrl`. The kit fills it from, in order:

1. the theme you pass (`product`);
2. the product's **registered presentation**, the `presentation` block of `.pkey/product` ([Presentation](/docs/build/manifest/product/#presentation-presentation)), served in the discovery document and read, verified and cached by the SDK;
3. the app bundle: `Info.plist`, the Android manifest, `package.json`'s `productName`, or Godot's `application/config/name` and icon.

With no icon at all, a kit draws a monogram tile, the product's initial on a neutral surface, never a Polaris Key mark. The accent follows the same order: yours, else the presentation's `accent` (its `accentDark` in the dark scheme), else a color derived from the icon, else a neutral ink.

Polaris Locker appears only in the optional "Powered by Polaris Locker" line or badge (`poweredBy`, off by default); Polaris Key appears only in two statements that are true about who handles a step: the sign-in footnote, and the device-code URL when the product sets no `deviceCodeUrl`. The service accents are off on product screens; opt in with `serviceCues: true`.

## The presentation default

Every kit has **one sign-in form**. Its body changes in place through Sign in, Finish in your browser (or the code), Choose a license (and Replace a device, when the license is full), and Done. No sheet or dialog stacks on it. Activation with a license key is a step of the same form, and also ships on its own for a key-only product.

One option sets where the form appears, with the same values in every kit:

| `presentation`       | The form                                                                                                                  |
| -------------------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `"inline"` (default) | In the screen or window pane the kit already owns                                                                         |
| `"sheet"`            | In one platform sheet or dialog that holds every step: a sheet on macOS, `ContentDialog` on Windows, `AdwDialog` on GNOME |
| `"browser"`          | The hosted sign-in card in the browser; the kit waits and moves on by itself                                              |

`replace` (`"inline"` or `"browser"`) does the same for Replace a device. Native controls stay native inside the form, including the system confirmation for a destructive Replace where the platform expects one.

## Accessibility

Kits target WCAG 2.2 AA in both themes: one heading per screen; visible labels on every field; errors announced and focused; modals that trap focus, restore it and close on Escape, B or back; layouts that survive the largest text size; keyboard, gamepad and D-pad reach; named icon-only controls; status never shown by color alone; and glass that turns opaque under reduced transparency.
